title: SiMa.ai closes $150m Series C at $1.45bn valuation
summary: Edge-AI chip maker SiMa.ai closed a $150m Series C taking its valuation to $1.45bn.

title: Anthropic draft S-1 leaks, showing steep losses ahead of IPO
summary: Fortune reports a draft Anthropic IPO prospectus has leaked and shows steep losses; no public S-1 had appeared on EDGAR as of late September, so the timetable remains open.

title: Moonshot AI files for Hong Kong IPO, seeking about $3bn
summary: Report says Moonshot AI, maker of Kimi, has confidentially filed for a Hong Kong IPO aiming to raise about US$3bn; listing targeted as early as Q1 2027 and a Shanghai STAR listing is also being weighed.

title: ServiceNow, SAP and Workday make AI agents pay to play
summary: PYMNTS reports the incumbents are charging external AI agents for access to their data and workflows, layering metered fees on top of subscriptions as seat counts come under pressure.

title: Firmus plans ASX IPO to raise about US$5bn at $31bn valuation
summary: Australian AI data-centre builder Firmus plans an ASX listing expected 22 October 2026, raising about US$5bn (A$7bn) at a $31bn valuation, the first large APAC public comp for AI infrastructure.

title: SpaceX discloses $60bn all-stock deal to acquire Cursor maker Anysphere
summary: A June 16 Form 8-K says SpaceX will buy Anysphere for about $60bn in stock, closing in Q3 pending regulatory approval, exercising an April option; announced days after its IPO.

title: DeepSeek prepares IPO, reportedly chasing about $71bn valuation
summary: DeepSeek is reported to be preparing a listing and seeking about $1.5bn of fresh funding at roughly $71bn weeks after its first outside round; a filing could come by end-2026.

title: PaleBlueDot AI raises $200m Series C at $3.2bn valuation
summary: PaleBlueDot AI raised a $200m Series C at a $3.2bn valuation, led by ComputeCore with B Capital participating.

title: Anthropic releases Sonnet 5.5, 30% faster and 30% cheaper for the work
summary: Weekly roundup reports Anthropic released Sonnet 5.5, promising about 30% faster speed at roughly 30% lower cost for the same work.

title: FTC opens broad probe of OpenAI, Anthropic and METR over agent incidents and safety claims
summary: Weekly roundup reports the FTC opened an investigation into whether agent incidents and safety claims could breach existing consumer-protection law; a voluntary White House safety accord was also signed.

title: Salesforce replaces Enterprise and Unlimited with Core, Advanced and Max editions bundling AI credits
summary: New Sales Cloud buyers choose Core ($195), Advanced ($395) or Max ($550) per user per month, each with an org-wide pool of Flex Credits for agents, moving AI cost from seat licence toward metered consumption.

title: OpenAI launches GPT-6.1 Sol and a $500 plan for high-demand users
summary: Weekly roundup reports OpenAI launched GPT-6.1 Sol, said to nearly match its top GPT-6 Astra at lower cost, plus an automated agent called Dots and a $500 plan for heavy users.

title: Atlassian evolves usage-based pricing for AI from 1 September
summary: Atlassian says it is expanding usage-based pricing as it adds AI capabilities, with customers given visibility and control over usage and spend.

title: Harvey raises $550m at $15.6bn valuation co-led by Lightspeed and Diffusion
summary: Harvey announced a $550m round, up from an $11bn mark in March; it reports ARR above $400m and more than 3,000 customers, and plans to build models in-house.

title: Google gives Gemini 4 Argon first to cyber defenders before paid API access
summary: CNBC asks whether Google's new Gemini 4 Argon can catch OpenAI and Anthropic at the frontier; roundups say it reached trusted defenders first and scored 68% on CWE-bench v1.

title: FTC chair Ferguson wary of AI firms seeking regulation plus antitrust exemptions
summary: FTC Chairman Andrew Ferguson said "regulation plus antitrust exemption sure sounds like moat-digging", responding to Anthropic CEO calls for antitrust permission for rivals to coordinate on AI pace.

title: Huawei Cloud takes CodeArts Agent to general availability in Singapore and Asia Pacific
summary: Huawei Cloud moved its multi-agent coding platform, 16 specialised agents across the software lifecycle, from public beta to commercial launch in Singapore after an open beta in Thailand in July.
